title: Engine integration tests - bypass null, Mix=0 passthrough, mono-lows invariant, walk bounds, tightness monotonicity, voice decorrelation, latency
description:
Add tests/EngineTests.cpp covering ShredDouble_Build_Spec.md §14 integration checks (items 3–5, 6–9, latency).

Before editing, inspect:
- tests/DSPPrimitiveTests.cpp style and helpers
- Source/DSP/ShredDoubleEngine.h and Voice getters
- .abracapocus/ShredDouble_Build_Spec.md §14 items 3–9 and §4.7–4.9

Implement assert-style tests:
1. Bypass null: with bypass engaged, output matches input sample-exact after accounting for reported latency (align by engine.getLatencySamples()).
2. Mix=0 passthrough: wet contribution silenced; dry path matches delayed original within tight tolerance.
3. Mono-lows invariant: below monoXover, output L≈R (shared-LP); use sine or noise LP-probed under crossover.
4. Walk bounds: after long process, Voice/engine-published tau_v stay in [10,35] ms and deltaC within configured ±pitch spread envelope (via MeterTap atomics or Voice getters exposed through engine).
5. Tightness monotonicity: RMS of tau/deltaC excursion decreases as tightness goes 0→100% with fixed spreads/rate.
6. Voice decorrelation: cross-correlation between isolated or pan-separated voice contributions stays below a loose threshold vs identical undiffused copies (or dual-engine/single-voice captures if engine exposes a test hook — prefer public APIs only; if needed, use extreme opposing pans V1/V2).
7. Latency: Studio reports 1024 samples and Live reports 256 (L/2 for L=2048/512), and setLatencyMode updates the getter.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: only tests/EngineTests.cpp. CMake registration is c.3.
